sources.finding: Government service S70787 tells covered electronic-communications service providers to inform CTU immediately about non-compliance, its nature/causes and corrective measures. It specifies ePortal form 5, data box a9qaats, or podatelna@ctu.gov.cz with a recognised electronic signature. This is company notification, not a generic enquiry or a consumer complaint.

Government service S70662 separately describes advance notification before providing a service relying on fundamental alteration/disproportionate burden. It requests description, reasons, unmet requirements and assessment date, with the same ePortal/data-box/signed-email options. It does not establish accepted reporting languages.

sources.finding: RRT distinguishes provider-first dispute resolution from reports of possible electronic-communications accessibility violations. For the latter it links to Konsultacijos. This supports the reporting purpose, not company/exemption filing.

The linked page (updated 26 August 2025) displays an enquiry form and expressly says it is unsigned, not a written application, and the response is an employee opinion rather than RRT's official position. An unsigned email receives the same caveat. Do not label this as a formal signed complaint route.

LRTK guidance associated with decision KS-37 of 23 April 2025 states that users may complain to LRTK after attempting resolution with the audiovisual-access service provider (paragraph 35); paragraph 30 requires exemption notification but gives no specific filing destination. These are guidance/powers, not evidence of an actual investigation. Recommendations are explicitly non-binding explanatory material.

General LRTK submission instructions list in-person/post/fax, lrtk@rtk.lt and an online form. The form asks programme/broadcast details and a security code. Its suitability for all EAA access-service cases and company exemptions is not demonstrated; no CAPTCHA, form or email was submitted.

next: Queue a scoped clarification of RRT's accessibility-report referral with its unsigned-enquiry caveat. Review LRTK general email/post against EAA complaint scope; do not promote its programme-oriented form or generic mailbox to verified company/exemption intake. LTSA routes and 112 oversight remain unresolved.
proposal: RRT public electronic-communications accessibility reports: link official accessibility guidance and Konsultacijos with the explicit unsigned/non-official-response limitation; keep formal complaints and company notifications separate.
